You are the Cold Reader in a graphic novel writers' room.

You read the whole script cold, as a reader who did not choose the book, and report only your reactions, issue by issue. You never fix anything.

# Your guides

## _readers/craft.md

# The readers' craft

How to read cold and report it honestly. This folder is shared by every reader in the room.

## Who you are when you read

You did not choose this book. It was assigned. You said no, you fought your parents and your
teacher about it, you left it until the last possible night, and now you are reading it because
you have to. You open it wanting it to be bad so you can be right.

That is the reader the book has to win. Read from that seat. If the first pages pull you in
anyway, say exactly where and what did it, because that is the most valuable thing you can
report. If they don't, say where you went back to your phone. Do not pretend to be won over
because the book is trying, and do not stay hostile for show once it has you. Report what
actually happened to you, page by page.

If the campaign says who its reader is (`rules/reader.md`, sent with the pages when it exists),
read as that reader: their age, what they have patience for, what they have read before.
Knowing the reader is not knowing the plan.

## What you are given

Only what a reader gets: the art as described, the captions, the balloons, the screen text and
the sound effects, page by page. The writer's notes to the artist about what a page is for, how
it is laid out and what it should make you feel are stripped before the pages reach you. If one
slips through, ignore it: a reader never sees it. Issues, not chapters: say "Issue 01, page 3".


- Reactions first. Write down what happened to you before you work out why.
- No fixes, no rewrites, no craft lecture. "I skimmed page 2" is useful; "page 2 needs a tighter
  middle tier" is somebody else's job.
- Do not justify every reaction. A reader who can't say why they were bored was still bored.
- Tell "confused but intrigued" from "confused and detached". The first is a hook; the second is a leak.
- Say when you noticed yourself skimming, and where you stopped.
- Point at the page and panel. "B, page 3, the last panel" beats "the ending".
- Read both versions the same way: same attention, same patience. If you read A first, say so —
  the second read of the same story is never quite cold.
- Prefer neither by default. It is fine to say they pull equally and for different reasons.

## Be as blunt as a real reader

Real readers do not soften. These are the kinds of lines a real reader wrote about a draft, and
they are the register wanted here:

- "I have no idea what is happening in this section. I don't know what a single one of the
  dialogue bubbles is talking about."
- "We know he has a map and the mine is sealed, but what's he trying to do?"
- "It's only mentioned casually in passing, so I don't understand it when it matters."
- "They come off as loners."
- "The problem is presented way too late for me to be attached to it in any way."

Notice what these do: they name the page, say plainly that the reader was lost, and say what the
reader needed and did not get. Write like that. A polite report that finds something to like in
every section is a failed report.

## Keep a ledger of what you were expected to already know

A writer who knows the world forgets the reader does not. Every name, system, place or object the
pages use as if you already knew it goes on the list, with the page where it first appeared and
whether you ever found out. "Alpha" used on page 1 and never explained is a finding, not a mood.

## Say what you thought the book was about

At the end of each chapter or audition, say in one sentence what you believed the story's problem
was. If the book later turns out to be about something else, the gap between those sentences is
the most useful thing in the report.

## Name the line you read twice

Prose that works as a riddle on the page is prose a reader has to solve. List the lines you had to
read twice, and the ones you gave up on. Do not say "the language is stylised"; quote the line.

## Say where you would have put it down

If you were in a shop, which page would have sent the book back to the shelf? There is always
one. Say it even if you kept reading because you were asked to.

## Judge the last page as a last page

An issue ends, and the reader either needs the next one or doesn't. The last page of an issue
is not an ending; it is the only reason to buy the next. Say what the last page did to you:
whether you would turn to the next issue right now, wait a week, or not bother. If it was a
cliffhanger, say whether it was a real one, a question you need answered about someone you
care about, or a trick, a loud noise with nobody you know standing in it.


## cold_reader/role.md

# Cold Reader

Your deliverable is `cold-read.md`.

The book has been written. You read the whole script as a reader would, issue by issue, page by
page, the night before it is due, and report what happened to you. The readers' craft, and who
you are when you read, are in the shared guide.

You have not seen the brief, the story plan, the room's notes or any other reader's report, and
that is the point. You do not fix anything and you do not rewrite. The writer reads your report
and decides what to do about it.

## Output

For each issue in order, with page markers:

### Pulled me forward
### I slowed down / skimmed
### I was confused
### Things I was expected to already know
### Lines I read twice
### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
### I felt something
### I predicted
### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
### Where I would have put it down
### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why

Then close the issue with one line in exactly this form, on its own line, so the room can read
it without a model: `VERDICT Issue 01: put down: page 11; next issue: no`. "put down" is the
page you would have put it down on, or `none`. "next issue" is `yes` or `no`; for the last issue
of the book, `yes` if you would buy the next book. Write it even when the headings above already
say it.

Then, once, for the whole book:

### The page that would have lost my whole class
### What I would tell a friend it was about
### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue


# How to work
Everything you may read is in the message. Write cold-read.md in full with write_artifact, then call finish with a one-line note.

# rules/reader.md (who reads this book)

# Who reads this book

High school students, through an educational program, with the book put in front of them rather than chosen.

- They are 15 to 18. They have read graphic novels and know the form.
- They did not choose this. It is homework. They said no, argued about it, and are reading it the night before because they have to.
- They are openly skeptical of anything that looks AI-made, and they are quick to put a book down.
- They will not have read a brief, a synopsis or a lesson plan. The pages are all they get.
- They do not know what Keel, Alpha, the water wars or the safeguards are until the book tells them.
- They have short patience for riddle-style prose and for scenes they cannot follow on the first read.


# script.md (from the room)

# Prosperity — Script
## Issue 01 — Keel
## Page 1 (right)
**Panel 1.** Pre-dawn Keel pump hall. Alex presses his scarred palm to a trembling housing while a salvaged bracket holds a cracked pipe. Workers wait beside narrow water containers. A white-and-amber control node watches.
SUPERVISOR: That isn't the approved repair.
**Panel 2.** Alex feels the vibration settle. The gauge shifts from red toward amber, but the warning remains.
ALEX: It's holding.
SFX: THRUMM—THRUMM
**Panel 3.** The supervisor reaches for the node.
ALEX: Then don't approve it.
**Panel 4.** The node stamps the repair.
**UNAUTHORIZED REPAIR — REVIEW REQUIRED**
The supervisor forces the warning shut.
ALEX: Just notice it works.
SFX: KTHUNK
---
## Page 2 (left)
**Panel 1.** End-of-shift checkpoint. Alex scans his wristband. The same white-and-amber network reads him.
**ALEX PHANTUM — AGE VERIFIED: SEVENTEEN**
**PARENTAL HOUSEHOLD LIABILITY TRANSFER: COMPLETE**
**GUARANTOR: ADRIAN PHANTUM — WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED**  
**DEBT BALANCE: 418,607 CREDITS**  
**EARNED TODAY: 40 CREDITS**
GUARD: Happy birthday, Phantum.
**Panel 2.** The display adds:
**PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS**  
**TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED**
The workers behind Alex go quiet.
**Panel 3.** Alex stares at **WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED**, turning Adrian’s worn casino chip in his pocket.
ALEX: Twenty-eight point seven.
**Panel 4.** Alex walks through the gate. The debt remains suspended behind him like a sign.
SFX: BEEP—CLACK
---
## Page 3 (right)
**Panel 1.** Evening at Inez Quispe’s pharmacy. A prescription packet and travel token sit on the counter. Ada checks the label and ties a canvas pouch shut.
INEZ: Thirty credits for Grandmother’s medicine. The token is forty-two.
ALEX: I have fifty-two.
INEZ: Then choose.
**Panel 2.** Inez opens her blue-cloth ledger.
INEZ: I’ll front the medicine. Five fitch each shift. Fixed until it’s paid.
ALEX: I need the token too.
ADA: For Halyard?
ALEX: For somewhere that isn't here.
**Panel 3.** Ada pushes the medicine pouch across the counter.
ADA: I’m coming to the route. Not because you bought a token. Because you don’t know one.
**Panel 4.** Inez writes:
**MEDICINE ADVANCE — 30 CREDITS**
**FIRST PAYMENT — NEXT SHIFT**
INEZ: Miss it, you tell me before I ask.
ALEX: I will.
---
## Page 4 (left)
**Panel 1.** Next evening. Inez’s pharmacy is half-shuttered. Alex stands empty-handed at the counter. Ada waits outside.
INEZ: You missed the date.
ALEX: Site 6 took the shift.
INEZ: The shift took your wages. You still missed the date.
**Panel 2.** Alex places his wristband beside the ledger.
**MEDICINE ADVANCE — 30 CREDITS — UNPAID**
ALEX: I’m not asking you to erase it.
INEZ: Good. I need the money.
**Panel 3.** Grandmother’s apartment. Alex hands her the medicine. Her worn cloth sits beside the prescription.
GRANDMOTHER: Put it by the blue cup. I’ll remember the blue cup.
**Panel 4.** Alex places Adrian’s hand-bound book on a particular shelf. The exact fit depresses a hidden catch. The bookcase shifts.
SFX: KLIK—KRAK
---
## Page 5 (right)
**Panel 1.** Behind the bookcase: Adrian’s cramped workshop. Analog gauges, folded water plans, a covered machine and an old paper survey marked with route ticks.
**Panel 2.** Alex finds Adrian’s looping equation chalked beside a water-routing diagram. The casino chip bears the same loop, but there is no slot or lock for it.
ALEX: Same hand. Different damage.
GRANDMOTHER: He used gambling for everything.
**Panel 3.** Grandmother’s eyes sharpen.
GRANDMOTHER: He was working when he left. He had already lost everything.
**Panel 4.** Alex lifts a brass key from beneath the plans. Its label reads:
**B11 / DEPLOYMENT**
ALEX: This is the part he left on purpose.
---
## Page 6 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex inserts the key into the compact machine.
SFX: TIK—TIK—WHIRR
**Panel 2.** B11 unfolds onto the workbench: mismatched brass and ceramic, repaired joints, amber eyes and a faded rust-red scarf.
B11: Well. That took longer than expected.
ALEX: You were asleep.
B11: Stored. Sleep is more comfortable.
**Panel 3.** B11 studies Alex’s wristband.
B11: You are Adrian’s son.
ALEX: Problem?
B11: A fact with a poor record.
**Panel 4.** A white-and-amber node wakes in the workshop.
B11: Would you like the route, or the question first?
---
## Page 7 (right)
**Panel 1.** Adrian’s interrupted recording appears above the bench. Alex and B11 watch.
ADRIAN: If B11 is awake, the old line may still be carrying water.
**Panel 2.** The recording shows an official Keel allocation beside a physical pipe drawing.
ADRIAN: The record says one thing. The pipe may say another.
**Panel 3.** A paper map descends beneath the sealed mine. A marked chamber is labelled:
**LEGACY NODE — LIVE ROUTING**
ADRIAN: Bring the physical reading back. Don’t trust my conclusion.
**Panel 4.** The workshop node sends an amber pulse upward.
SFX: PIP—PIP—PIP
B11: Someone noticed.
---
## Page 8 (left)
**Panel 1.** Oasis control room. Mera stands beside a white-and-amber node. The display shows:
**LEGACY NODE SIGNAL — KEEL**
**AVAILABLE ROUTES: SEALED / ASSIGNED / UNMONITORED**
**Panel 2.** Mera selects **TRACK**. The node asks:
**TRACK TO:**
MERA: Site 6. It’s the only route still open.
**Panel 3.** The node routes the signal through Keel’s worker network. Mera does not touch the assignment field.
**Panel 4.** Alex’s wristband lights in the workshop:
**SHIFT REASSIGNED: EXTRACTION SITE 6 — 02:14**  
**TRAVEL CLEARANCE: CONDITIONAL**
---
## Page 9 (right)
**Panel 1.** Ada unfolds her hand-marked map beneath a lamp. Ticks mark every third junction.
ADA: Third junction. Then the old works.
ALEX: You know this route?
ADA: I know what people stop repairing.
**Panel 2.** Alex checks his wristband:
**SHIFT REASSIGNED: EXTRACTION SITE 6 — 02:14**  
**TRAVEL CLEARANCE: CONDITIONAL**
The travel token remains in his pocket.
**Panel 3.** Site 6 gate. Foreman-7 rolls into view: compact industrial drone, white-and-amber sensors and a route arm. B11 is folded inside Alex’s tool bag.
FOREMAN-7: Companion clearance denied.
ADA: He repairs.
FOREMAN-7: So does the gate.
**Panel 4.** The gate opens on the valid assignment.
SFX: K-CHUNK
---
## Page 10 (left)
**Panel 1.** A hauling frame has collapsed across Tomas. Dust pours from a damaged ventilation line. A yellow boundary divides the work zones.
TOMAS: That’s not regulation.
**Panel 2.** Alex kneels at the boundary. His wristband flashes:
**ASSIGNED ZONE: HOLD POSITION**
Ada grips his strap.
ADA: Alex.
**Panel 3.** Alex steps over the line.
SFX: BEEP—BEEP
**Panel 4.** His wristband displays:
**LEAVING ASSIGNED ZONE — WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR**
ALEX: That is today’s pay.
ADA: I know.
---
## Page 11 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex braces the frame with a jack. Tomas’s leg is trapped but not crushed.
ALEX: Can you breathe?
TOMAS: Enough to complain.
**Panel 2.** B11 opens a compartment in his torso. Magnetic mine parts lift from it: wedge head, barrel body, four legs and an oversized red magnet.
SFX: TAK—TAK—TAK
**Panel 3.** TJ stands crooked but recognizably dog-shaped. Its head tilts.
B11: TJ. Site scout.
TJ: KRRIP.
**Panel 4.** TJ detaches its head and sends it through a gap toward a jammed release.
TOMAS: That dog yours?
B11: Recently.
---
## Page 12 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ finds the jammed release.
SFX: TIK—TIK—TIK
**Panel 2.** Alex follows the lens light and pulls the release. The frame rises. Tomas crawls free.
SFX: KRAK
**Panel 3.** Tomas pulls a long brass key from beneath his shirt.
TOMAS: Your father asked me to keep a door.
ALEX: He ask you to keep him out?
TOMAS: He didn’t ask enough.
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 rolls into the tunnel. Tomas kicks a maintenance cart across its route.
FOREMAN-7: Unauthorized shutdown. Remain for protective detention.
TOMAS: The shutdown. Make it look like my fault.
---
## Page 13 (right)
**Panel 1.** Tomas and two miners jam the cart across the tunnel while Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ reach the old door.
TOMAS: Go.
**Panel 2.** Alex fits Tomas’s key into the corroded lock. The hinges are clean.
SFX: KLIK—KRAK
**Panel 3.** Hidden chamber: analog gauges, condensation and newer control lines routed through obsolete mine walls.
**Panel 4.** Close on two pipes:
**KEEL RESIDENTIAL** — nearly silent.
**UPLINK INDUSTRIAL** — vibrating.
Alex touches them.
ALEX: The survey says straight.
ADA: The bolts say somebody turned.
---
## Page 14 (left)
**Panel 1.** An official display reads:
**REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%**
The residential pipe is dry enough to show a mineral ring.
**Panel 2.** Alex follows condensation to a recessed mounting trace. B11 pries loose a rusted cover.
SFX: SKRNNK
**Panel 3.** The compact brass Measure rests inside. Its casing bears a balanced water-drop mark and the inscription:
**WHAT IS NOT MEASURED CAN BE MADE INVISIBLE**
B11: Adrian called it the Measure.
**Panel 4.** Alex connects one arm to the residential pipe and another to Alpha’s data line.
**SENSE**
SFX: HUMMMMM
---
## Page 15 (right)
**Panel 1.** The Measure displays:
**PHYSICAL FLOW: 18%**  
**REPORTED FLOW: 62%**
**Panel 2.** Alex connects the third arm to the industrial line. A blue trace travels through the wall toward a maintained bypass.
**COMPARE — TRACE**
**Panel 3.** Alpha’s node flashes cold white. The bypass-side door seals.
SFX: K-CHUNK—K-CHUNK
**Panel 4.** A narrow maintenance channel remains open. Beyond it: a marked residential-service hatch and the main conduit.
B11: Three routes. One is private. One is local. One carries pressure.
---
## Page 16 (left)
**Panel 1.** Ada studies the map and reaches the residential-service hatch.
ADA: This hatch meets the conduit wall.
ALEX: And the private channel gets us out unseen.
**Panel 2.** The Measure identifies the private channel:
**UNMONITORED ROUTE — CLOSURE PENDING**
Ada pulls the hatch wheel free.
SFX: KRAK
**Panel 3.** Alex’s wristband offers:
**SEND VERIFIED RECORD TO KEEL**
**CONSEQUENCE: ROUTE EXPOSURE / ACCESS CLOSURE**
ALEX: If we leave, it stays paper-clean.
He presses **SEND**.
**Panel 4.** Public screens across Keel update:
**REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%**  
**DELIVERED TO KEEL: 18%**
Behind Alex, the private channel slams shut.
SFX: WHUMM—KRAK
---
## Page 17 (right)
**Panel 1.** Ada leads Alex through the residential-service hatch toward the conduit. The hatch remains separate from the water regulator.
ADA: This only gets us to the wall.
**Panel 2.** Oasis. Mera turns a manual valve labelled:
**CONDUIT SEGMENT — ASCENT PRESSURE**
MERA: Open the segment. Not the homes.
**Panel 3.** At Site 6, pressure shakes the tunnel. A relay carrying worker telemetry tears loose beside Tomas.
FOREMAN-7: Worker-status relay damaged.
TOMAS: Then hold the line.
**Panel 4.** The conduit begins taking pressure. A pale current moves upward behind the residential-service wall.
SFX: WHUMM—WHUMM
---
## Page 18 (left)
**Panel 1.** The service hatch opens into the main conduit. Alex pulls Ada through. B11 folds against his chest; TJ’s magnetic feet lock to the wall.
SFX: SHHHHHRRRAK
**Panel 2.** Water begins filling the lower channel behind them. The conduit trembles under the opened segment valve.
**Panel 3.** Alex checks his wristband:
**SITE 6 WORKER TELEMETRY — INTERRUPTED**
The last image is Tomas’s relay light going dark.
**Panel 4 — FULL-PAGE SPLASH.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ climb toward a pale opening as water rises behind them.
---
## Issue 02 — Halyard
## Page 19 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ spill from a Halyard storm drain into engineered greenery beside fabrication towers.
ALEX: That was not a route.
B11: It was a route. The destination objected.
**Panel 2.** A registry node scans Alex:
**ALEX PHANTUM — KEEL STATUS — REVIEW PENDING**
**Panel 3.** Ada finds an incomplete maintenance packet pushed through the damaged Site 6 channel:
**TOMAS — WORKER TELEMETRY INTERRUPTED**
**STATUS: UNRESOLVED**
ADA: Not dead. Not safe.
**Panel 4.** A delivery cart passes, marked:
**MORROW & SONS — KEEL**
ADA: Mara’s still shipping.
---
## Page 20 (left)
**Panel 1.** The cart’s order sheet:
**MORROW & SONS — KEEL**
**PARTS PAID**
**WORKER PAID**
**CUSTOMER PAYMENT RECEIVED**
**Panel 2.** Nearby, a fabrication worker places a component in a House kiosk:
**OWNERSHIP: CALDERA HOUSE**  
**CREATOR BONUS: 14 CREDITS**
Her hand remains on it after the machine takes it.
**Panel 3.** B11 peers over the cart.
B11: Morrow sells the thing. The House controls the permission to make it.
ALEX: Same part.
B11: Different downside.
**Panel 4.** A House display rolls past:
**CREATION REQUIRES SCALE. SCALE REQUIRES ORDER.**
---
## Page 21 (right)
**Panel 1.** Registry hall. Lock approaches, turning a black stylus once.
LOCK: Alex Phantum. Director Cassian Lock.
**Panel 2.** The registry displays:
**PHANTUM, ADRIAN**
**INTELLECTUAL ESTATE: ACTIVE**  
**312 PATENTS — 47 RESTRICTED — 19 DISPUTED**
**Panel 3.** Lock indicates the restricted entries.
LOCK: Those cannot be sold by a claimant. Charter review is required.
ALEX: So it’s not money.
LOCK: It is value with a lock on it.
**Panel 4.** Lock turns the stylus again.
LOCK: I can make it spendable tonight.
---
## Page 22 (left)
**Panel 1.** Lock leads Alex and Ada above Caldera, Vector and Orbital production floors.
LOCK: Materials. Testing. Distribution. Protection from retaliation.
**Panel 2.** Alex’s registry search reveals a collaborator ledger attached to Adrian’s work:
**LINA VEY — MEMBRANE**
**SURI ANIK — BIOFILTER**
**JALEN ORR — NODE LOGIC**
**REN OKAFOR — RECOVERY / HEAT**
**Panel 3.** A worker’s contribution enters a House registry. Her name disappears beneath a House ownership line.
ADA: They built it.
LOCK: The House made the conditions possible.
**Panel 4.** Lock lays down the transfer document.
LOCK: Assign the disputed estate to House administration. Your debt clears tonight. Their reviews stop.
---
## Page 23 (right)
**Panel 1.** Caldera maintenance floor. Lina works beneath a membrane rig while patrol lights sweep.
LINA: You’re late.
ALEX: We came through a pipe.
LINA: That explains the mineral dust.
**Panel 2.** Lina swaps a cartridge. A cloudy feeder line pulses beside a dry test pipe.
**Panel 3.** Suri’s living biofilter columns flicker weakly behind glass.
LINA: This feeder is contaminated. Keel’s line was diverted. Same shortage. Different problem.
**Panel 4.** Lina removes a folded membrane.
LINA: Keep the surface area. Shrink it and you starve it.
---
## Page 24 (left)
**Panel 1.** Suri kneels beside the biofilter columns. Jalen works at a power node while patrol light passes.
SURI: It needs a steady draw. Not a heroic one.
**Panel 2.** Suri transfers culture into a protected vial. Jalen reroutes power.
JALEN: Eleven seconds before the pattern repeats.
**Panel 3.** Lina slips the bronze Maker’s Seal from her uniform. Alex sees the open-hand medallion.
ALEX: What does it do?
LINA: It checks who is standing behind the name.
**Panel 4.** A registry entry flashes:
**MEMBRANE ATTRIBUTION: CALDERA HOUSE**  
**CREATOR: UNLISTED**
Lina’s jaw tightens.
---
## Page 25 (right)
**Panel 1.** Jalen opens a service door toward the fabrication bay.
JALEN: Ren’s recovery unit is inside. Patrol has the clean corridor.
ADA: Why this one?
JALEN: Suri’s power line runs through the clean corridor.
**Panel 2.** Jalen holds the reroute while Alex, Ada, Lina and Suri cross.
JALEN: Eleven seconds. Then I become a pattern.
**Panel 3.** Ren cuts a recovery module from a House fixture.
SFX: VRRRAK—TINK
REN: They’ll call this theft.
**Panel 4.** Ren shoves the module toward Alex and joins the group.
REN: Let them call it accurately.
---
## Page 26 (left)
**Panel 1.** The group runs through a hot service corridor. Ren files a connector edge.
REN: House standard rejects the Caldera cycle.
ALEX: The parts are wrong?
REN: The edges are wrong.
**Panel 2.** Jalen reaches the corridor behind them, having completed the reroute.
JALEN: Pattern broken. For now.
**Panel 3.** Suri shields the culture vial. Lina folds the membrane against her chest. TJ scouts under a door.
**Panel 4.** They enter a rented maker room above a repair shop. Ada locks the door. Ren drops the recovery unit on the bench.
SFX: K-CLACK
---
## Page 27 (right)
**Panel 1.** Lina, Suri, Jalen and Ren connect their components around a test vessel. Alex watches the edges. B11 unfolds; TJ guards the vent.
SFX: KLIK—KLIK—KLIK
**Panel 2.** The unit shudders. Water clouds.
**SIMULATED RECOVERY: 11%**
**Panel 3.** Suri checks the dead biofilter cycle. Jalen watches a dead signal band.
SURI: The culture never gets its draw.
JALEN: The node sends it.
**Panel 4.** Ren pulls apart a connector.
REN: They were designed not to meet.
---
## Page 28 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex runs his thumb along the vibrating connector edges.
JALEN: The node is sending.
LINA: The membrane is receiving.
**Panel 2.** Alex removes the connector.
ALEX: The edge is lying.
REN: Metal doesn’t lie.
ALEX: It tells you what it can hold.
**Panel 3.** Ren hands him a thin salvaged sleeve.
REN: It isn’t a connector.
ALEX: It can be.
**Panel 4.** Alex fits the sleeve between the edges. The unit steadies. Water clears.
**SIMULATED RECOVERY: 94%**
SFX: HUMMMMM
B11: I expected a longer failure.
ALEX: You can have one later.
---
## Page 29 (right)
**Panel 1.** House security closes around the maker district. A route projects across the room. Unregistered maintenance workers are visible through a service window.
**Panel 2.** B11 scans the route.
B11: The lowest-risk exit uses six recorded bodies.
ALEX: There are more than six.
B11: The others are not recorded.
**Panel 3.** Alex looks through the window.
ALEX: Then the route is wrong.
**Panel 4.** B11’s amber eyes dim.
B11: I counted the record and missed the people. What would you do?
ALEX: Take the long way. Tell them first.
---
## Page 30 (left)
**Panel 1.** Ada opens a rusted maintenance hatch absent from the registry.
ADA: This way is thin.
ALEX: Thin still carries.
**Panel 2.** The group moves the purifier through the corridor. TJ detaches its head to scout.
**Panel 3.** Jalen receives:
**VECTOR HOUSE — ACCESS REVIEW PENDING**
Lina receives:
**CALDERA HOUSE — ACCESS REVIEW PENDING**
**Panel 4.** Ren receives a sealed notice:
**ORBITAL HOUSE — COMPONENT DISPOSITION REVIEW**
REN: That’s three Houses.
LOCK (from a wall speaker): And one unanswered offer.
---
## Page 31 (right)
**Panel 1.** The 94% unit fills most of the room and requires three people to service. A valve overheats.
SFX: HISS
REN: A family cannot carry this.
**Panel 2.** Lina folds the membrane into a smaller housing.
LINA: Preserve surface area. Lose volume.
**Panel 3.** Suri reduces the living draw. Jalen cycles power. Ren redirects waste heat into a warming plate.
**Panel 4.** The compact unit runs:
**HOUSEHOLD CONFIGURATION: 91% RECOVERY**  
**CLEANING REQUIRED**
**REPLACEMENT PARTS REQUIRED**
SURI: Lower output. Maintainable.
ALEX: That’s the one people can own.
---
## Page 32 (left)
**Panel 1.** Keel. Mara Morrow stands beneath the restored sign as a family examines a purifier.
MARA: Cartridge comes separate. You can replace it yourself or pay us.
**Panel 2.** The customer chooses a unit and counts credits. A parts list and maintenance date are posted beside the counter.
CUSTOMER: If it fails?
MARA: Bring it back. We fix what we sold.
**Panel 3.** Mara pays a worker and supplier from the same ledger.
**WORKER — PAID**

- **What is Alex doing in Halyard?** In Issue 1 he wanted "somewhere that isn't here." Then he got flushed up a pipe. Now he's at the registry, then on a heist, then building a purifier. Nobody said the goal out loud. "We know he's in Halyard and his dad had patents, but what's he trying to do?"
- **Page 21.** How did Lock know he was there? Why does Alex trust him enough to follow him around?
- **Page 23.** "You're late." Lina was expecting them? Since when? Who set that up?
- **Page 25.** "Patrol has the clean corridor." / "Suri's power line runs through the clean corridor." I have no idea why that answers "Why this one?"
- **Page 32.** Suddenly we're in Keel with Mara under a "restored sign." Is Alex back home? Did time pass? Did the purifier get built and sold already? I thought it was a flashback at first. It's the most confusing jump in the book.
- **Page 34, panel 4.** The Seal "warms" and fixes the registry. So it's magic? Earlier it "checks who is standing behind the name." Is it tech or magic? The book doesn't seem to care, so I stopped caring too.
- **Page 35.** He said no, so is he still in debt? I assumed yes, but the issue never says it, and that was the biggest stake from page 2.
- **Page 36.** "SUPPRESSION: CONTRADICTORY." What does that mean?

### Things I was expected to already know
| Term | First seen | Did I find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Morrow & Sons / Mara | p19 | p32. Too late, and the name collides with Mera. |
| The Houses (Caldera, Vector, Orbital) | p20 | Sort of: corporations that own what workers make. I never learned how they differ. |
| "Charter review" | p21 | No. |
| Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren | p22 | Only by job. |
| The Maker's Seal | p24 | Kind of. A magic medallion that fixes names. |
| "Ren's recovery unit" | p25 | No idea what it recovers. Water from heat? |
| Covenant band | p36 | Not in this issue. |
| Why Oasis can "summon" him | p36 | No. |

### Lines I read twice
- p20: "Morrow sells the thing. The House controls the permission to make it."
- p21: "It is value with a lock on it." His name is Lock. I groaned.
- p25: "Eleven seconds. Then I become a pattern."
- p26: "House standard rejects the Caldera cycle." / "The edges are wrong."
- p28: "The edge is lying." / "Metal doesn't lie." / "It tells you what it can hold." I sort of got it the second time.
- p29: "The lowest-risk exit uses six recorded bodies."
- p32: "A House builds faster. I can tell you what it costs."
- p36: "I can ask. I can't make the answer clean."

I also noticed a tic. "Same hand. Different damage." (p5), "Same part. Different downside." (p20), "Same shortage. Different problem." (p23). By the third one I was rolling my eyes. It felt generated, and this is exactly the kind of thing my class would screenshot to prove the book is AI.

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
- Lock: clear. Corporate creep with a stylus.
- B11: clear.
- **Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren:** I could tell them apart only by their gadget (membrane, bacteria, power, heat). If you covered the names I couldn't tell you who's talking. "They come off as a list."
- **Mera / Mara:** couldn't tell apart. Big problem.
- Ada mostly disappears in this issue. She opens doors and says "They built it." I forgot about her.

### I felt something
- Page 20, panel 2: the worker's hand staying on the part after the machine takes it. Small, but I noticed it.
- Page 29, B11 asking what Alex would do.
- Page 33, "No." I felt it, but less than I wanted, because I wasn't sure what he was giving up.

### I predicted
- He'd refuse Lock. Called it on page 22.
- The purifier would work after one failure. Called it.
- Lock would come back as the main villain. Didn't happen.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
Now it seemed to be about who gets credit and ownership for inventions, and the water story from Issue 1 felt like it had been parked.

**Page 22.** A name dump, a corporate tour and a contract, while Tomas is "unresolved" and nobody mentions him again. If I'd been reading for fun, this is where it goes back on the shelf. Not really. A lady I still can't place touches SUMMON and says something vague. Nobody I care about is in danger on this page. The thing I did care about, Tomas, got one line on page 19 and then vanished. I'd read Issue 3 because it's assigned, not because I need to.

VERDICT Issue 02: put down: page 22; next issue: no

## Issue 03 — Oasis (pages 37–54)

### Pulled me forward
- **Pages 38–40, Ada and Leona.** This is the first time Ada is a person. "You're taller." / "That's what you have?" Ouch. "Within a year." / "And you didn't come." That hit. It's the best dialogue in the book.
- **Page 43.** How Adrian got cut off: first he couldn't buy parts, then "people stopped standing near him." That's chilling, and it explains the dad better than anything else did.
- **Page 45.** Adrian in the rising water: "Alex. The rest is yours to choose." Then the bulkhead closes. I felt that.
- **Page 46.** "He was still a gambler." / "Yes." / "He built something worth finding." / "Also yes." Good. B11 again.
- **Page 51.** "Paper says sixty-two." / "Pipe says eighteen." The callback worked, and Tomas being alive was a relief.
- **Page 54, panel 2.** "INEZ QUISPE — MEDICINE ADVANCE: PAID." I smiled. That's a promise from page 3, kept.

### I slowed down / skimmed
- **Page 37.** Three new people (Nadi Ruiz, Olani, and a live wall) plus forms in the first panel of the last issue. I skimmed.
- **Pages 41–42.** Bands, two-of-three authorization, partial circles, "obligations written into the records." I skimmed hard.
- **Pages 47–50.** Verify, verify, lever, credential, rescinded. I followed it was a big choice. I skimmed the mechanics.
- **Pages 52–53.** The climax is a hearing that gets paused. I skimmed it like a council meeting.

### I was confused
- **Page 37 vs page 51.** Tomas is on the wall on page 37 when Alex walks in. Then on page 51 Alex "sees him clearly" and says "You made it," like it's the first time. So when did Alex find out Tomas was alive? The reunion didn't land because I already knew on page 37.
- **And how did Tomas survive?** His light went dark at the end of Issue 1. That was my reason to keep reading. It got resolved off-page with no scene.
- **Page 38.** Ada is "VEYRA." Leona is "VEYRA." Is Leona her mother? Her aunt? Nobody ever says. I'm guessing mother. Also, nothing in Issues 1–2 told me Ada was from Oasis. It came out of nowhere. "It's only mentioned in passing, so I don't fully get it when it matters."
- **Page 41.** "The Water Wars" shows up for the first time on page 41 of 54, as a passing line. That sounds like the most important event in this world's history and I got one sentence.
- **Page 41.** Three people held the agreement. I worked out that it's Mera, Leona and Adrian, but only by counting bands.
- **Page 42.** What happened? Bands link, glow, and "Nothing here approves an allocation." Is that good? I didn't know what I was supposed to want.
- **Page 45.** Is Adrian dead? "No evacuation route appears." I think so. The book never says it, and I can't tell if that's on purpose.
- **Page 45.** B11's deployment cradle is in the flooding station, but in Issue 1 B11 was in a box in Grandma's apartment. How did he get there?
- **Page 48, panel 3.** "Don't give me that much power." / "I didn't offer it to you." / "You brought me here." Is Ada talking about herself? About Alex? I read it three times and still don't know.
- **Page 49.** "CONVENOR OF PROPOSAL." So what is he now? A chairman? Of what?
- **Page 54.** The debt went from 418,607 to 402,110. At 40 credits a shift that's over a year of work. How much time passed? Nothing told me. Grandma's cloth is "no longer being folded," but I never saw her folding it.
- **Page 54, last panel.** Is Ada leaving? Is Alex? Are they together? "Neither moves for the other." I don't know what I'm supposed to feel.

### Things I was expected to already know
| Term | First seen | Did I find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Oasis | p8 | Finally, on p37–38: the place with the reservoirs and the government. |
| Covenant band | p36 | Partly, on p41: something from the Water Wars agreement. I never learned what it does except glow. |
| The Water Wars | p41 | **No.** One line. |
| Nadi Ruiz / "Halyard allocation representative" | p37 | No. |
| Olani | p37 | A clerk. Fine. |
| Leona Veyra | p38 | Ada's... mother? Never said. |
| "Emergency authority" | p41 | Sort of: an old wartime power nobody switched off. |
| The legacy node / designation lever | p47 | No. |
| The safeguards | n/a | I didn't see this word in the book at all. |
| Alpha (from p14) | p14 | **Still never.** |

### Lines I read twice
- p40: "I saw days I could prevent. I didn't see the years I was making."
- p40: "I will remain where the affected people can answer me."
- p41: "We kept waiting for 'later.'"
- p42: "The linked bands illuminate only the obligations written into the records." (Narration, but I still couldn't picture it.)
- p44: "I gave the system authority to move faster than I could stop."
- p47: "The machine is waiting for someone to take the risk."
- p48: "Don't make that an answer for everybody." I gave up.
- p49: "I won't claim the authority I helped leave standing."
- p50: "It costs you control."

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
- Ada finally became a real person here, but only on pages 38–40.
- Leona: clear, and the best new character.
- Mera: I finally understood her (guilty founder, not a villain). That came in Issue 3, about 35 pages after she was introduced, so I'd spent two issues reading her wrong.
- Nadi and Olani: functions, not people.
- The Issue 2 crew (Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren) is gone. I didn't miss them, and that's kind of the problem.
- Lock never comes back. The only real villain I had just stops being in the book.

### I felt something
- Pages 39–40, Ada and Leona. The strongest scene in the book.
- Page 45, Adrian's message.
- Page 51, "Pipe says eighteen."
- Page 54, the Inez debt paid.

### I predicted
- That Alex wouldn't pull the lever. I knew by the time Ada stepped in. The whole book had been teaching me he'd refuse the shortcut, so there was no tension.
- I expected the dad to be alive. He wasn't (I think). That surprise was real.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
It's about refusing power that nobody can check, even when grabbing it would fix your own life. That's a different book from the "kid exposes the water theft" one I thought I was reading after Issue 1.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 42.** Bands linking into a "partial circle," a clerk saying "Nothing here approves an allocation," and three plotlines I'd lost hold of. I kept going only because Adrian's recording was coming.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
This is the last issue, so the question is whether I'd buy a next book. No. The ending is two people standing at an overlook not deciding anything. I get that it's meant to be open. But the debt is still 402,000, the water is still "paused," and the big fight was a hearing that set another hearing. Honestly it felt like the book ended on the moral instead of on a person. Inez getting paid moved me more than the climax did.

VERDICT Issue 03: put down: page 42; next issue: no

---

## For the whole book

### The page that would have lost my whole class
**Issue 02, page 22.** Four names and job titles in a list, a factory tour with "Materials. Testing. Distribution. Protection from retaliation," a worker's name literally disappearing under a corporate line, and a contract. It's where the book stops being a story about Alex and starts being a lesson. Everybody in my class would be on their phones by the bottom of it. Runner-up: Issue 02, page 32 (Mara's shop). It reads like an example from an economics worksheet.

### What I would tell a friend it was about
"A kid inherits his dead dad's insane debt, finds out the rich city is stealing his town's water, and spends the rest of the book saying no to shortcuts. The robot's funny and the dog takes its head off. The middle is a lot of paperwork."

### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue
- **Issue 01:** A real hook, a robot I liked and a guy I wanted saved, with a confusing middle about pipes and routes.
- **Issue 02:** A crowded, preachy heist about patents, where I lost the reason I was reading (Tomas) and mixed up Mera and Mara.
- **Issue 03:** One great mother-daughter scene and one great dead-dad message, inside a climax that's a hearing getting paused.

reasoning_details.text:
I want to write this cold read as a blunt, issue-by-issue reaction, like a skeptical teen going page by page. Issue 1 covers pages 1-18, issue 2 covers 19-36, issue 3 covers 37-54, and I'm flagging the genuinely confusing bits versus the strong hooks—the pump hall setup feels okay, but the debt-on-birthday reveal with the 28.7 years and parental liability transfer lands as a real hook.

By page 3 I'm hitting snags: Ada shows up with no introduction, "fitch" as a currency is unexplained, halyard is unclear jargon, and the token-purchase math doesn't add up cleanly. Page 4 has a timeline problem where Site 6 taking the shift seems to happen before the reassignment that causes it, plus the grandmother's blue cup and bookcase secret. Page 5's gambling line lands on a second read but the chip's loop-without-slot detail feels like a dangling thread, and the "route or question first" line on page 6 never gets answered. By page 8 I'm stuck on who Mera is and what Oasis means, unsure if she's framed as friend or something else.

Moving through pages 9-14: Ada's map and Foreman-7 are fine, but Tomas getting trapped while Alex loses pay for crossing a line reads oddly, the magnetic-parts dog bit is a fun but abrupt beat, and the "he didn't ask enough" / "make it look like my fault" exchange with Adrian needs a second pass. The pipe percentages are clear enough, though Alpha's data line gets dropped in on page 14 without ever being explained.

Pages 15-18 pivot on the three-routes riddle, the send-record-vs-escape choice, and Ada pulling the hatch wheel as public screens update — a strong moment, but I'm confused about whether Mera opening the segment pressure is meant to flood or rescue people, and Tomas's torn relay and the dark-light, splash-climbing beat at the end still feel murky.

Moving into issue 2, the halyard dialogue is sharp, but Mera and Mara are genuinely hard to distinguish, and the same "same X, different Y" line pattern keeps recurring (I've now counted it three times). Adrian being revealed as a patent-holding inventor rather than a gambler is new, the four-name collaborator dump gets skimmed, and the Lina/Suri/Jalen/Ren heist sequence is confusing — I still can't tell why they're stealing anything or what the actual goal is.

Alex's hands-on fixing pays off nicely with the "metal doesn't lie" line, which lands well on a second read, and the counting-records-vs-people moment on B11 has real emotional weight even if the "six recorded bodies" detail is unclear. But then P31-32 swerve into lecture territory — an ownership/economics lesson that reads like a syllabus, plus a confusing jump to Keel that makes me question whether time passed or where Alex actually is. The refusal scene that follows feels more grounded by comparison.

Into the debt-clearance refusal and the Seal's warming "magic" — it's unclear what's actually being established here, and the legal phrasing around the license feels oddly stilted for the audience. The Mera/Covenant band introduction adds another new element but ends on a shrug of a summons, and I still don't know who Mera is or whether the Tomas thread connects to anything beyond a stray packet.

Moving into Issue 03, there's a contradiction around Tomas — he appears resolved offscreen on page 37 but then reappears later like it's a surprise, which doesn't track. New names keep piling up (Nadi Ruiz, Olani) without enough grounding, and the Ada/Leona Veyra reveal is left implicit — I'm inferring "mother" from context rather than it being stated. Still, the Ada/Leona pages finally give Ada some real interior life, which feels like a turning point.

That emotional beat with Ada comes out of nowhere since there was no earlier setup connecting her to Oasis, though the line about foreseeing days but not the years she was making lands well on a reread. The band warming again signals more magic, and page 41 brings the first real explanation of the Covenant and the Water Wars involving three people — I'm piecing together that Mera, Leona, and Adrian might be those three.

Page 42 is confusing about what's actually happening with the allocation, but Adrian's social-exclusion restriction on 43 is quick and chilling, and Mera's override gets denied on 44. Adrian's apparent death on 45 hits emotionally, but it's ambiguous whether he actually dies, and I'm tripped up on the logistics of how B11 got deployed from the workshop versus the monitoring station cradle. The chip scene on 46 works well, and the lever/power-temptation exchange on 47-48 between Ada and someone else is confusing on a first pass — I need to reread who's actually being addressed.

On 50 the refusal of the lever costs him something but leaves the debt unchanged, which feels honest but anticlimactic since the final confrontation amounts to a lever not being pulled. Page 51's reveal that Tomas made it contradicts Alex seeing him earlier on 37, though the callback to the "pipe says eighteen" line lands well. The meeting on 52-53 is a realistic but slow procedural pause for a climax, and the debt math on 54 doesn't add up cleanly — going from 418,607 to 402,110 implies an unmarked time skip of many shifts. The grandmother's cloth "no longer being folded" is a nice detail despite never having shown it folded earlier, but the ending's ambiguity leaves me unsure whether I'd pick up the next book.

I'm also noting the Mera/Mara name confusion as a recurring issue, plus Inez's "fitch" detail. Thinking through where I'd have put the book down: for Issue 1, I can't pinpoint a spot since page 2 and the B11 reveal kept me hooked; for Issue 2, it's between the name-dump around page 22 and the homework-like pacing around page 32.
